source_refs.note: ii. Substitution reaction: a main subheading of 22.4 Reactions of Alcohols, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 92-92.

blocks.text: In the substitution of alcohols, a hydroxy group (-OH) is replaced by another substituent (e.g. halogens) to form a new product (e.g., halogenoalkanes). The substitution of different halogens with the –OH group is given in the following reactions.

blocks.prompt: a) Write chemical reaction of propan-1-ol with SOCl₂.
b) Differentiate the reaction of PCl₃ and PCl₅ with propan-1-ol with the help of the chemical equations.
blocks.explanation:
PCl₃: 3CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + PCl₃ → 3CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + H₃PO₃
PCl₅: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + PCl₅ → CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + POCl₃ + HCl

rows: one PCl₃ reacts with three alcohol molecules
one PCl₅ reacts with one alcohol molecule

blocks.prompt: c) How ethanol reacts with KBr? give reaction equation.
blocks.explanation:
With concentrated sulphuric acid: the acid and KBr together form HBr, which replaces the -OH of ethanol by Br:
CH₃CH₂OH + KBr + H₂SO₄ → CH₃CH₂Br + KHSO₄ + H₂O
